reviews.label: good
reviews.reason: Recovered all 61 protected Python modules (404 code objects; 359 encrypted instruction regions) and inspected security-relevant disassembly. The backend implements local coding-agent sessions, editor/MCP tools, model requests, and user-facing terminal execution, with a loopback default listener and tool-confirmation flow. No dedicated attack functionality, credential theft, persistence, or covert command channel was identified. Full archive scan emitted 61 recovered children and no hostile findings. The two retained suspicious findings describe actual PyArmor protection and native runtime debugger checks.

classification_history.label: inconclusive
classification_history.reason: CodeGeeX VSIX bundles PyArmor 9.1.8-encrypted Python modules and native runtime debugger checks. Wrappers and package metadata were inspected, but the protected backend logic could not be recovered with the available static analysis; no clear endpoint judgment is justified.

label_policy_notes: Exploits, exploit PoCs and dedicated exploitation/post-exploitation toolkits are bad, including authorized research and test implementations
The four dual-use artifacts are bounded security probes, exposed-file scanning, and offline password-auditing/hash conversion; none is treated as good training data
CodeGeeX was corrected to good after static recovery of every protected Python module; its protection findings remain visible. See pyarmor-recovery.json.
